To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

older and younger adults benefit equally from multisession, dual task practice in a PRP paradigm, and that the practice/training benefits of the older adults are as large as those of the younger adults.

1) older adults have larger psychological refractory period effects than younger adults; 2) older and younger adults show similar benefits of practice; 3) the benefit of practice is not due to the practice of the task that shows a larger psychological refractory effect; and 4) the benefit of training is due to the training of the task with the larger psychological refractory effects, not the smaller ones.
